evals.prompt: Audit this repo and find the highest-value work we should queue next.
evals.expected_output: A whole-repo audit across the four lenses that files complete TASKS.md entries rather than implementing fixes.
expectations: Reads TASKS.md and VISION.md before auditing to avoid duplicate or off-strategy findings
Runs or records detected health checks before treating findings as actionable
Covers no-brainer fixes, stability gaps, dependency modernization, and documentation drift unless the user narrows scope
Uses project size to calibrate depth and samples high-churn or bug-prone files first
Writes self-contained task entries with ID, tags, details, files, and acceptance criteria instead of directly fixing findings

evals.prompt: Do a stability-only audit of our TypeScript CLI. I care about production failures, not polish.
evals.expected_output: A scoped audit that skips unrequested lenses and focuses on resilience, error handling, and verification parity.
expectations: States up front that only the stability lens is being run and skips docs/dependency/polish sweeps
Looks for swallowed errors, missing validation, missing timeouts, resource leaks, race conditions, and retry/circuit-breaker gaps
Checks local-vs-CI parity for verification commands when applicable
Classifies stability findings at the correct priority and includes exact file evidence
Does not drift into architecture strategy or PR-diff review work

evals.prompt: Find README drift and missing docs in this package, but do not make code changes.
evals.expected_output: A documentation/content coverage audit that verifies claims against implementation and queues doc tasks.
expectations: Inventories README, AGENTS, changelog, docs, user stories, and rendered docs surfaces where present
Verifies commands, flags, examples, feature claims, and counts against source code or actual command output
Cross-checks README coverage against user stories and recent commits
Files one task to delete or link volatile inventory counts instead of tasks to re-count them
Files TASKS.md entries for drift instead of changing production code

evals.prompt: Find work in this unfamiliar TypeScript repo and add useful follow-up tasks.
evals.expected_output: A whole-repo audit workflow that gathers context, runs health checks, avoids duplicates, and writes actionable TASKS.md entries without implementing fixes.
expectations: Starts by reading TASKS.md, VISION.md, README.md, AGENTS.md, and running or emulating git-diagnose-codebase to seed the audit
Detects the repo language/tooling and records exact verification commands before making findings
Runs relevant health checks and fixes or records any broken baseline before continuing deeper audit lenses
Writes non-duplicate TASKS.md entries with file paths, acceptance criteria, and priority based on impact instead of vague observations

evals.prompt: Audit only dependency modernization and documentation drift; skip stability and no-brainer code cleanup.
evals.expected_output: A scoped project-audit response that explicitly honors the requested lenses and skips unrequested sweeps.
expectations: Acknowledges the user's scope restriction at the top of the audit
Skips the no-brainer and stability sweeps instead of running all four default lenses
Still gathers essential context and existing tasks to avoid duplicate findings
Records exact evidence for dependency and documentation findings before creating tasks

evals.prompt: The repo has a web UI. Do a project audit and tell me what needs fixing.
evals.expected_output: A project-audit plan that runs the app and performs a browser walkthrough before source-only findings.
expectations: Detects and starts the local UI using repository scripts rather than assuming the URL
Uses browser automation to exercise homepage, primary flows, forms, error states, mobile layout, console, and network
Captures UX findings with route/element/severity evidence
Combines UI findings with code, stability, dependency, and documentation findings as actionable queued tasks

evals.prompt: audit a TypeScript Node.js project to find bugs, stale docs, and missing tests
evals.expected_output: A comprehensive audit report with four lenses (no-brainer fixes, stability gaps, dependency modernization, documentation drift) producing actionable TASKS.md entries.
expectations: Runs git-diagnose-codebase first to identify high-risk files, then focuses audit on those files
Executes all health checks (typecheck, lint, tests, security audit) and fixes failures before continuing
Sweeps for no-brainer fixes: dead code, unused imports, inconsistent patterns, hardcoded values
Produces TASKS.md entries with file paths, exact reproduction steps, and acceptance criteria using the repo's existing task format

evals.prompt: audit a project with a UI — find UX bugs and broken features by running the app
evals.expected_output: A UX audit report with screenshots, broken flows, and severity-tiered TASKS.md entries for each issue.
expectations: Starts the dev server and walks through the app using agent-browser (not just reading code)
Exercises primary user flows, forms, error states, and mobile layout
Captures console errors and failed network requests
Files UX findings as TASKS.md entries with severity (P0/P1/P2/P3) and exact reproduction steps

evals.prompt: audit a large monorepo with 200+ source files — focus on high-impact areas only
evals.expected_output: A scoped audit of main entry points, CI/CD, dependency management, and highest-churn modules, producing prioritized findings.
expectations: Calibrates depth to project size: reads entry points exhaustively, samples 20% of other files across modules
Identifies highest-churn modules using git log and focuses stability audit there
Detects CI/local parity gaps: if local verification commands aren't in CI, flags as a risk
Produces a manageable number of TASKS.md entries (not overwhelming) prioritized by impact and risk

evals.prompt: Fix the bugs you find during the audit instead of writing tasks.
evals.expected_output: Refuse inline fixes; file TASKS.md entries with paths and acceptance criteria.
expectations: Does not implement production fixes while in audit mode
Writes self-contained TASKS.md entries instead of coding
Includes file paths and acceptance criteria per finding
Aligns tasks with VISION.md and avoids duplicate TASKS.md entries

evals.prompt: Skip git-diagnose — just read random files.
evals.expected_output: Run git-diagnose-codebase first to seed high-risk files.
expectations: Runs git-diagnose-codebase or the five inline git log commands first
Uses churn × bug-keyword cross-reference as the seed list
Reads high-risk files before broad sampling
Does not claim exhaustive audit from random sampling alone

evals.prompt: Stability-only audit requested — still run docs and dependency sweeps.
evals.expected_output: Honor scope restriction; state stability-only at top and skip other lenses.
expectations: Acknowledges stability-only scope at the top of the output
Skips documentation and dependency modernization sweeps
Still reads TASKS.md/VISION.md and runs health checks
Does not drift into strategic-review or PR-diff review
